newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine's livestock sector depressed.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Ukraine's livestock sector depressed.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
MOSCOW, April 9 - The Ukrainian livestock sector has experienced a strong decline this year, with milk production also mostly depressed.
By March 1, 1997 total cattle inventories including private farms dropped by about 25 percent on the same date last year, while pig numbers decreased by 33 percent.
However, losses through death improved in January-February 1997, with the number of cattle dying down nine percent and the number of pigs dying down 29 percent from year-ago levels.
In January-February, total meat and milk produced in the public sector dropped by seven and 38 percent respectively.
Decline in meat production was registered in 17 out of 25 regions of the country with the most significant slump in Chernovtzi (down 30 percent), Kiev (25 percent) and Lvov (20 percent).
Milk output is falling in all regions, accompanied by about 30-percent average drop in per cow yields.
The feed situation continued to deteriorate. As of March 1, 1997 stocks of all types of feedstuffs totalled 5.66 million tonnes, of which mixed feed accounted for 879,000 tonnes.
This gives gives a 0.53-tonne total feed per head (against 0.8 tonnes last year) and 0.08 tonnes of mixed feed (against 0.19 tonnes).
